- **Nine months 2025 (2025-10-30):** the story was "resilience plus digital." Revenue was stable, TF1+ (the group's free streaming platform) advertising was up 41%, and net cash was EUR 465M. The first crack came at the end of the call: the political crisis in France had hit October advertising, and the 2025 margin target was cut from "broadly stable" to 10.5%-11.5%.
- **Full year 2025 (2026-02-12):** the tone shifted from "a temporary air pocket" to an admission that something structural had changed. The CEO, Rodolphe Belmer, said viewing time among the target audiences is falling about 10% a year, and, crucially, that TF1 can no longer fully offset that with price increases because its return on advertising spend is now "more or less similar to YouTube." Price increases would be "low to mid-single-digit... rather than two-digit level that we had before."
- **Half year 2026 (2026-07-30):** the narrative contracted to "protecting profitability." Advertising revenue fell 9%, group revenue fell 6% like-for-like, and the headline wins were cost agility and a better-than-feared operating profit (EUR 77M). The growth story moved to the Netflix distribution deal (live since 18 June 2026) and micro-payments, both still too young to show up in revenue.

The arc: from "we are outperforming a soft market" to "the market is structurally declining and we are managing the decline well."
